title: Cokret Grant Constraint
$comment: Property ordering is grouped by constraint family to match capabilities.md §6 (the human-readable family map): discriminator/meta, then temporal, field_access, type_restriction, scope_limitation, delegation_control, quota, claim_based, confidentiality, then the moderation cache-invalidation hint. Canonical JSON re-sorts keys lexicographically so this ordering is presentation-only and does not affect the wire (see C13-07).

constraint_id.description: Optional stable identifier of this constraint within the grant; used for diagnostics and overrides.

constraint_type.description: Constraint family discriminator. v1 collapses what were 15 types into 8 by absorbing narrowly-scoped types into their conceptual parent: edit_window → temporal; container_move → scope_limitation; rate_limiting + resource_limit → quota; approval_workflow + accountability + device_session → claim_based (with subtype); encryption_requirement + visibility_control → confidentiality (with subtype). Use the optional 'subtype' field to indicate the original specialization where evaluation logic differs.

evaluation_class.description: Cacheability/dependency hint for the authorization evaluator. stateless = pure function of (constraint, op, now); grant_local = depends on the grant object only; realm_state = depends on Realm frontier (membership, policy_version, etc.); external = depends on data outside the Realm causal frontier (claim revocation status, rate-limit history counts, async approval). Each constraint_type has a canonical evaluation_class declared in constraint-schema.md §2.3; implementations MAY tighten (e.g. grant_local → stateless) but MUST NOT loosen (e.g. external as stateless). Auth evaluators SHOULD use this hint to gate fast-path caching.

subtype.description: Optional discriminator within a constraint_type. Standard values: claim_based.{claim,approval,accountability}; quota.{rate,resource}; confidentiality.{encryption,visibility}; temporal.{window,edit_window,redact_window,session}. Per constraint-schema.md §2.2, device/session binding is NOT an independent subtype: it is the claim_based subtype=claim sub-case expressed via claim issuer = device cross-signing key. Implementations MAY require subtype for these families and fail closed on unknown values.

applies_to_actions.description: Optional restriction of a temporal constraint to specific capability actions (e.g. ['ck.message.revise.own', 'ck.message.redact.own']).

recurrence.description: Recurrence rule for temporal constraints. Used by constraint-schema.md §3.1.

expires_after.description: ISO 8601 duration; used by approval_workflow constraint instead of expires_after_ms.

condition.description: Conditional predicate for field_access and similar constraints. The `kind` value is a registered named condition from constraint-schema.md §4.1; unknown kinds MUST fail closed. Implementations MUST NOT introduce ad hoc string DSL predicates.

allowed_space_kinds.description: Allowed Space kinds (e.g. 'board', 'list', or profile-registered kinds like 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket'). Reducer/profile MUST validate kind value.

allowed_circle_ids.description: Limits Circle-scoped capability actions to the listed Circle ids. Used by ck.circle.manage / ck.circle.member.manage style grants; unconstrained Realm-wide Circle management grants are not a normal permission shape.

allowed_session_ids.description: Limits agent interop-session status/result/cancel delegation to the listed ck:agent_interop_session ids.

blob_presign_scope.description: Scope limiter for ck.self.blob.command.presign grants: allowed purposes plus optional blob/realm restrictions.

allowed_data_classes.description: Data classification labels this grant may read, export, transform, or send to external endpoints.

allowed_endpoints.description: Allowed outbound endpoint origins or deployment-approved endpoint patterns for applet / agent / connector operations.

max_delegation_depth.description: Maximum remaining delegation hops. Bounded by the canonical delegation chain depth ceiling (4) defined in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md §3 and zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.2; reducers MUST reject grants declaring a larger value at accept time rather than only truncating during DFS.

blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum TTL, in seconds, that this grant permits for ck.blob.presign. The service must clamp requested max_age_seconds to the smaller of this value and deployment policy.

max_artifact_bytes.description: Maximum artifact size in bytes for applet / agent / export operations.

requires_claims.description: Conditional claim requirements. resource-selector-grammar.md §3.3 caps this array at 32 entries as a normative DoS guard; the schema enforces maxItems:32 so condition-selector grants cannot smuggle in unbounded claim objects.

subject_matches_actor.description: If true, the credential subject DID MUST match the actor DID.

value_constraints.description: Per-field equality / membership constraints on credential claims.

min_encryption_level.description: confidentiality(subtype=encryption) static floor: the minimum content-encryption mechanism the grant requires. Values mirror Realm/Circle encryption_profile. Pure static declaration evaluated as stateless unless cross-checked against the Realm's current encryption_profile (see constraint-schema.md §12).

allow_plaintext_fallback.description: confidentiality(subtype=encryption) static flag: whether the grant permits plaintext when the encryption floor cannot be met. See constraint-schema.md §12.

require_audit_trail.description: confidentiality(subtype=encryption) static flag: whether the grant requires an audit trail (e.g. active Audit Applet Binding). See constraint-schema.md §12.

depends_on_moderation_state.description: Cache-invalidation hint: when true, this grant's authorization decisions depend on the ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell (see policy-server.md §7.1 and capabilities.md §18.1) and the grant's cache entry MUST be invalidated when that cell changes. Default false: ordinary grants (ck.strand.update / ck.message.create / org membership grants) do NOT take a cache hit on every moderation decision. v1 capabilities.md §18.1 lists three conditions where MUST be explicitly true (moderator-role grants, condition-selector subjects referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue / cell). Schema-side enforcement of condition (2) is in capability-grant.schema.json via if/then on actions[]; conditions (1) and (3) are reducer-side lint. Cache invalidation hint outside the eight constraint families; it does not participate in allow/deny evaluation and is documented in capabilities.md §6 / constraint-schema.md.

allOf.$comment: constraint-schema.md §2.2 / §2.3: claim_based, confidentiality and quota families have NO valid no-subtype form — every row in the §2.3 evaluation_class table carries a subtype (claim/approval/accountability; encryption/visibility; rate/resource). Without this gate a {"constraint_type":"claim_based","effect":"allow"} with no subtype passes schema validation, letting weak implementations cache an external (claim-revocation) constraint on the grant_local fast path (see C05-03 fail-open). temporal is intentionally excluded: a temporal constraint with no subtype is the valid ordinary time-window form.
